data.question_title: The best way of understanding our own civilization is to take an ordinary sort of day in the life of an ordinary sort of man, myself for instance, and to see what he does. My home is in London. I get up in the morning when an alarm clock rings on the table by my bed. It is quite a complicated machine and works perfectly. I get into a hot bath, the water for which has been heated by gas. The gas is supplied to me by the gas board for the area in which I live; it is part of the national system. The water for the shave comes from a kettle which has been heated by electricity. As far as I am concerned, what happens is very simple: I put a plug in the wall and put on the switch and the electricity does the rest. I use a safety razor, the blade of which is made of very finely tempered steel, has been cut, together with millions of other blades, by machines. The clothes, which I put on, have also been spun and woven largely by steam or electrically driven machines.
